The implementation is complete, but I'm unable to build and run the tests — shell commands that compile or build are being denied by the permission system in this session (only read-only commands like `ls` are allowed).

## What I implemented

**`kindergarten_garden.h`** — declares the `Plants` enum (`clover`, `grass`, `violets`, `radishes`) and the function `std::array<Plants, 4> plants(const std::string& diagram, const std::string& student)`.

**`kindergarten_garden.cpp`** — the solution:
- The student's position is derived from the first letter of their name (`student.front() - 'A'`), since all twelve students start with A–L in alphabetical order.
- The diagram is split on the `\n` into two rows; each student occupies columns `2*index` and `2*index + 1` in each row.
- A small `plant_for` helper maps `G`/`C`/`R`/`V` to the enum values.
- Returns `{row1[c], row1[c+1], row2[c], row2[c+1]}` — first row (nearest the windows) first, left to right, matching the expected ordering in the tests.

I verified the logic by hand against every test case (single-student gardens, Bob/Charlie on `VVCCGG`, and all twelve students on the 24-cup garden, including Larry at the last column).

To run the tests once you have shell permissions enabled, from the exercise directory:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DEXERCISM_RUN_ALL_TESTS=ON
cmake --build build
./build/kindergarten-garden
```
